questions: Where do you live? What do you like about it?
Do you prefer living in a flat or a house? Why?
What would you change about your neighbourhood?
What do you usually do at the weekend?
Tell me about a hobby you have.
What did you do last weekend?
What are you studying? Why did you choose it?
What would your ideal job be?
How do you usually prepare for exams?
Where did you go on your last holiday?
What kind of holiday do you prefer? Why?
Which country would you like to visit in the future?

part2.title: Part 2 – porównaj dwie sytuacje (opis słowny zamiast zdjęć)

cards.a: A family having a picnic in a park
cards.b: A group of friends eating in a restaurant
cards.question: Why might the people have chosen to eat in these places?

cards.a: A student studying alone in a library
cards.b: Students working together on a project in a classroom
cards.question: How might the students be feeling?

cards.a: A person running along a beach at sunrise
cards.b: A group of people playing basketball in a gym
cards.question: What are the advantages of exercising in these ways?

cards.a: A tourist taking photos in front of a famous monument
cards.b: A tourist relaxing in a hotel pool
cards.question: Why might people choose these kinds of holiday?

cards.a: A chef cooking in a busy restaurant kitchen
cards.b: A person cooking dinner at home for their family
cards.question: What might be difficult about these situations?

cards.a: A person working at a laptop in a café
cards.b: A person working in a crowded open-plan office
cards.question: Which might be better for concentrating, and why?

tasks.central: A school is planning to organise an event to raise money for charity. Talk about how good each of these ideas would be, then decide which would raise the most money.
tasks.decision: Which would raise the most money?

tasks.central: A town wants to encourage young people to spend more time outdoors. Talk about the advantages of each idea and decide which is the best.
tasks.decision: Which is the best idea for the town?

tasks.central: Some students want to improve their English over the summer. Talk about how useful each way would be, then decide which is the most effective.
tasks.decision: Which is the most effective way?

questions: Do you think young people should be encouraged to do charity work? Why?
What is the best way to persuade people to give money?
Is it better to give time or money to a charity?
How can schools help students to care about others?
Do you think people spend enough time outdoors these days?
What are the benefits of spending time in nature?
Why do some people prefer to stay at home?
How can cities provide more green space?
Why is it important to learn foreign languages?
Is it better to learn a language at school or abroad?
Do you think everyone will speak English in the future?
What helps you to learn languages effectively?
